study.title: Matthew 4: Jesus" victory in the wilderness, the beginning of the Kingdom, and the call of the first disciples
study.overview: Matthew 4 presents Jesus overcoming temptation in the wilderness, publicly beginning his preaching in Galilee, calling disciples to follow him and confirming his message with teaching and healing. The chapter shows that his mission is not born of human prestige, but from obedience to the Father: he rejects power shortcuts, fulfills the Scriptures, proclaims repentance and brings together a people around the Kingdom of heaven. The movement of the chapter is clear: from loneliness and spiritual combat to the formation of a community of followers and for a ministry marked by word and compassion.

outline.title: Jesus is tempted and won by the faithful use of Scripture
outline.explanation: The Spirit leads Jesus to the desert, where he fasts, feels hungry and faces the devil in three assaults: to use power to supply himself, test the divine protection and worship Satan in exchange for the kingdoms of the world. In each answer, Jesus quotes Scripture and refuses any path that deviates from obedience to the Father. The text culminates in the removal of the devil and the service of angels.

outline.title: Ministry begins in Galilee with prophetic fulfillment and call to repentance
outline.explanation: Upon learning of John's prison, Jesus settled in Capernaum, and Matthew sees in this the fulfillment of Isaiah about the light that visits the people in darkness. The initial message of Jesus is simple and decisive: repent, because the kingdom of heaven is near.

outline.title: Called the first disciples
outline.explanation: Jesus calls Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John, while working. The call is immediate and requires concrete rupture: they leave nets, boats and even the father to follow Jesus. The image of "fishers of people" shows that their mission will come to bring people together for the Kingdom.

outline.title: Teaching, preaching and healing attract crowds
outline.explanation: Jesus travels to Galilee teaching in the synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom and healing all sorts of sickness. His fame spreads across large regions, including outside Galilee, and crowds follow him. The chapter ends by paving the way for the teaching that will follow.

study.context: The chapter is at the beginning of Jesus" public ministry, shortly after the testimony of John the Baptist and the temptation in the desert. The text shows Jesus acting first in Galilee, with emphasis on Capernaum, and mentions the presence of people from various regions, including areas linked to Judea, the region beyond the Jordan and the Decapolis. The notes also highlight that the reference to Syria indicates the wide repercussions of Jesus" fame.
study.theology: Matthew 4 presents Jesus as the obedient Son who triumphs where the people of God failed. The notes compare his experience to that of Adam and Israel: he faces the sinless test and confirms his faithfulness to the Father. The chapter teaches that true sonship is not used for self-promotion, but for obedience; therefore Jesus rejects the misuse of power, the way of spectacle, and false worship. The centrality of the Word of God also stands out: Jesus responds to temptation with Scripture, shows that life depends not only on material sustenance and teaches that worship belongs only to the Lord. The beginning of preaching announces the heart of the gospel of the kingdom: repentance. The call of the disciples reveals that following Jesus implies concrete renunciation and participation in his mission. The healings confirm the authority of the Kingdom and the compassion of the Messiah, who unites teaching, proclamation, and restoration.

scholarViews.insight: The temptation of Jesus presents him as the second Adam and the second Israel; he overcomes Satan and demonstrates perfect obedience to the Son of God.
The preaching of Jesus begins with the message of repentance, and that is the standard for every messenger sent by God.
The final verse should be linked to the next chapter, as the great multitudes anticipate the immediate continuation of the narrative.

questions: What shortcuts of power, success or security can I turn away from obedience to God, as the proposals made to Jesus in the wilderness?
How does repentance appear in practice as the proper response to the closeness of the kingdom of heaven?
What does it mean today to leave nets, boats or legitimate occupations to follow Jesus with real priority?
study.practice: In this chapter, concrete application is to learn to respond to temptation with the Word of God, not with personal impulses or justifications. We are also called to take repentance seriously, assessing whether our life already fits the coming Kingdom. Finally, the call of the first disciples asks for a practical answer: to obey Jesus above security guards, routines and bonds that compete with his priority. Followers of Christ must unite listening, renunciation and participation in their mission to proclaim and serve.
study.uncertainty: The given notes do not clarify in detail the exact chronology between the temptation and the immediate beginning of preaching in Matthew, nor do they allow to affirm with historical precision all the places mentioned beyond what the text itself and the commentators observe. Nor is there a sufficient basis to define with certainty the exact geographical scope of expressions as "all the realms of the world" in Satan's speech; therefore, this passage should be dealt with caution, recognizing the possibility of visionary or broad language, as suggested in the notes.
